title: Terraform in the pipeline: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI and a reviewed plan

videos.script: Every lesson so far ended with Ana typing terraform apply on her laptop. It worked, and it hid a lot. {{laptop}} Terraform plans the files in the directory, not a commit. A change nobody reviewed can reach production from one terminal. {{diff}} This lesson moves the apply to one place: a pipeline. A pull request gets checked, scanned and planned, and the plan is posted where reviewers read the diff. {{flow}} After the merge, the plan is made again and saved to a file. A person reads that file, approves it, and exactly that file is applied. {{saved}} You will write the pipeline twice, for GitHub Actions and for GitLab CI. Neither can run here, so the steps live in one script, and that script runs for real. {{script}} The pipeline gets into AWS with no stored key. Each job proves who it is with a short-lived token, and only an approved job can write. {{oidc}} And you will watch two runs race for one state. Terraform refuses the plan that went stale, and a queue stops the race before it starts. {{race}}
